title: Descent of base-open factorization along a representable surjective scheme chart
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], let $Y$ be an algebraic space over $S$, and let $q:h_U\to Y$ be a representable surjective morphism from an $S$-scheme $U$, in the scheme-test sense of [def-trf-algebraic-space], within [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $W\subseteq S$ be any open subscheme with inclusion $j:W\hookrightarrow S$ [def-weil-open-immersion]. If the structural map $U\to S$ factors through $j$, then the structural map $Y\to h_S$ factors uniquely as $Y\xrightarrow{b}h_W\xrightarrow{h_j}h_S$. In scheme-test terms, for every $a:h_T\to Y$ the structural scheme morphism $T\to S$ factors uniquely as $T\xrightarrow{b_a}W\xrightarrow{j}S$, and for every scheme-test morphism $r:T'\to T$ one has $b_{a\circ h_r}=b_a\circ r$. These factorizations define the natural transformation $b$. No affineness of $U$ or $W$, and no etaleness of $q$, is required.

proof.text: Fix a scheme test $a:h_T\to Y$, and write $f_T:T\to S$ and $f_U:U\to S$ for the structural maps. By the scheme-test definitions of representability and surjectivity in [def-trf-algebraic-space], $h_T\times_Yh_U$ is represented by a scheme $P$, and its projection $p:P\to T$ is surjective. The other projection gives $v:P\to U$; explicitly a natural map $h_P\to h_U$ gives its scheme map by evaluation at $\mathrm{id}_P$, and naturality identifies its value at $r:V\to P$ with $v\circ r$. All maps are over $S$, so $f_T\circ p=f_U\circ v$.

source.place: Tag 03FY, lemma-union-of-quasi-compact, final proof sentence; scheme-test expansion using Tag 025V, definition-relative-representable-property, in spaces.tex.

proof.text: Choose the assumed factorization $u:U\to W$ with $j\circ u=f_U$. For every point $t\in T$, surjectivity of $p$ gives a point $z\in P$ with $p(z)=t$. Hence $f_T(t)=f_U(v(z))=j(u(v(z)))\in W$. Thus $f_T(T)\subseteq W$. This argument concerns underlying points, so it does not require a section of $p$ or an etale or flat hypothesis on $q$.

source.place: Tag 03FY, lemma-union-of-quasi-compact, final proof sentence; scheme-test expansion using Tag 025V, definition-relative-representable-property, in spaces.tex.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] to the scheme morphism $f_T:T\to S$ and the open subscheme $W\subseteq S$, using the image containment just proved. It supplies a unique scheme morphism $b_a:T\to W$ with $j\circ b_a=f_T$.

source.place: Tag 01HI, lemma-restrict-map-to-opens, with the whole source open; Tag 01IK, lemma-open-subspace-scheme.

proof.text: Let $r:T\prime\to T$ be a scheme-test morphism. The two maps $b_{a\circ h_r}$ and $b_a\circ r$ into $W$ have composites with $j$ equal to $f_{T\prime}$, since $f_T\circ r=f_{T\prime}$. The uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme], applied to $f_{T\prime}$, gives $b_{a\circ h_r}=b_a\circ r$.

Construct $b$ on sections explicitly. For $y\in Y(T)$, define $a_y:h_T\to Y$ by $a_y(V)(s)=Y(s)(y)$ for $s:V\to T$. Define $b_T(y)=b_{a_y}\in h_W(T)$, with $h_W(T)=\operatorname{Mor}_S(T,W)$ as in [def-trf-algebraic-space]. The identity $a_{Y(r)(y)}=a_y\circ h_r$ and the preceding step give $b_{T\prime}(Y(r)(y))=b_T(y)\circ r$, so these functions form a natural transformation $b:Y\to h_W$. Its composite with $h_j$ is the structural transformation, since $j\circ b_{a_y}=f_T$. Any other such transformation has, on every $y\in Y(T)$, a scheme map $T\to W$ lifting $f_T$; uniqueness in [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-factors-through-open-subscheme] forces it to equal $b_T(y)$. This proves uniqueness of $b$. For an arbitrary $a:h_T\to Y$, naturality gives $a=a_{a(T)(\mathrm{id}_T)}$, so the construction recovers precisely its stated $b_a$.

lean.statement: theorem surjective_chart_base_open_factorization {S : Scheme.{u}} (Y : AlgebraicSpace S) (U : Over S) (q : yoneda.obj U ⟶ Y.obj.obj) (hq : IsSurjective q) (W : Scheme.{u}) (j : W ⟶ S) [IsOpenImmersion j] (hU : ∃ c : U.left ⟶ W, c ≫ j = U.hom) : ∃ b : Y.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk j), b ≫ yoneda.map (Over.mkIdTerminal.from (Over.mk j)) = ((Over.mkIdTerminal (X := S)).isTerminalObj yoneda _).from Y.obj.obj ∧ (∀ b' : Y.obj.obj ⟶ yoneda.obj (Over.mk j), b' ≫ yoneda.map (Over.mkIdTerminal.from (Over.mk j)) = ((Over.mkIdTerminal (X := S)).isTerminalObj yoneda _).from Y.obj.obj → b' = b) ∧ (∀ (T : Over S) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y.obj.obj), (yoneda.preimage (a ≫ b)).left ≫ j = T.hom ∧ ∀ c : T.left ⟶ W, c ≫ j = T.hom → c = (yoneda.preimage (a ≫ b)).left) ∧ (∀ (T T' : Over S) (r : T' ⟶ T) (a : yoneda.obj T ⟶ Y.obj.obj), (yoneda.preimage ((yoneda.map r ≫ a) ≫ b)).left = r.left ≫ (yoneda.preimage (a ≫ b)).left)
